Fixes for adding -Od (#3292)

A customer couldn't recompile their large shader with -Od for debugging in PIX.
-The symbol manager would quit early, so now it continues to discover other variables
-The value-to-declare pass was adding an incorrect debug location, which tripped up the verifier.

$ git --no-pager show ac5630e8e^:lib/DxilPIXPasses/DxilDbgValueToDbgDeclare.cpp | findstr /n GetVariableLocation   [the location the pass attached, pre-fix]
llvm::DILocation *VariableRegisters::GetVariableLocation() const
{
  const unsigned DefaultColumn = 1;
  return llvm::DILocation::get(
      m_B.getContext(),
      m_Variable->getLine(),
      DefaultColumn,
      m_Variable->getScope());
}

llvm::Value *VariableRegisters::GetMetadataAsValue(

WHAT THAT MEANS
  DILocation::get(ctx, line, column, scope) is the 4-argument overload: InlinedAt is null.
  So for a variable declared in a function that -Od left as a real call but that the PIX
  passes see through inlining, the pass attached to an instruction in the *entry* function a
  !dbg whose scope chain terminates in the *callee's* DISubprogram, with no inlinedAt: to
  make that legal. That is exactly what llvm::Verifier::visitDISubprogram rejects with
  "!dbg attachment points at wrong subprogram for function".

  The shape matches the dump in the issue line for line:
    reported  !970 = !DILocation(line: 96, column: 1, scope: !965)   ; !965 = DILexicalBlock
    pre-fix   DILocation::get(ctx, m_Variable->getLine(), /*column*/ 1, m_Variable->getScope())
  column: 1 is not a column the front end would emit for a declaration; it is DefaultColumn
  in the code above. No inlinedAt: in either.

CURRENT STATE at ab5400907 (lib/DxilPIXPasses/DxilDbgValueToDbgDeclare.cpp)

  the call site now uses the originating instruction's own DebugLoc:
  1231:   auto *Expression = GetMetadataAsValue(
  1232:       GetDIExpression(Ty, sizeOverride == 0 ? offsets.Aligned : offsets.Packed,

  1235:       m_B.CreateCall(m_DbgDeclareFn, {Storage, Variable, Expression});
  1236:   DbgDeclare->setDebugLoc(m_dbgLoc);

ANCESTRY

$ git merge-base --is-ancestor ac5630e8e HEAD   -> exit 0  (0 = the fix is in the triaged build)
$ git rev-list --count v1.5.2010..v1.6.2104     -> 268 commits in the window, 3 of which
  touch the pass (listed at the top). Of those 3, only ac5630e8e changes the debug location
  attached to the synthesised llvm.dbg.declare; the other two add handling for ray query
  handles and for language features, and neither calls setDebugLoc.

STRENGTH OF THIS ATTRIBUTION

  Strong, not certain. The behaviour change was measured on release binaries either side of
  the window (manual-case-history.txt); the commit was not built and run in isolation, so
  this is source reasoning over a 268-commit window narrowed to one plausible commit, not a
  bisect. The commit message independently describes the same failure mode ("The
  value-to-declare pass was adding an incorrect debug location, which tripped up the
  verifier"), and its author is the person the issue tells you to ask for details.
